purpose: Real result of dispatching .github/workflows/biotech-sponsor-scan.yml, connecting Milestone 3 Phase C's classifiers to the 6 of this project's own 23 accepted issuers whose real SEC-registered SIC code puts them in drug or medical-device development (config/m3-biotech-sponsor-map.json). Updated in place from this same day's first dispatch (run #2, commit b531b93) after adding device-clearance coverage (nre.device_clearances) and closing LNSR's own zero-FDA-coverage gap -- superseded rather than left beside it, since both records describe the same workflow's current, real behavior.
independent_cross_check: Every number above was separately reproduced by hand (plain urllib, not this project's code) against the live APIs on 2026-09-30 before each dispatch: NBIX's 4 FDA-drug matches are INGREZZA, INGREZZA SPRINKLE and CRENESSITY (x2 submissions) under openFDA's own short sponsor_name 'NEUROCRINE'; COLL's 4 are XTAMPZA ER, NUCYNTA (x2) and NUCYNTA ER under 'COLLEGIUM PHARM INC'; TECX/ASMB/ACHV's 0 FDA-drug matches were confirmed as real HTTP 404 zero-result searches, consistent with all three being clinical-stage with nothing FDA-approved yet; LNSR's 4-of-5 clinical-trials match is the same 4 real 'LensAR Incorporated' studies found by hand, with the 1 non-match being a real but unrelated 'Center For Sight' study. LNSR's 14 fda_devices matches were independently reproduced by hand the same way just before this dispatch: 14 real 510(k) records under applicant 'Lensar, Inc.' (all matching), 0 real PMA records (a genuine HTTP 404 -- LNSR has never had a Class III device requiring Premarket Approval).
context: None of the 68 events in config/m2-combined-events.json is itself a clinical-trial-result or FDA-action announcement -- every one is a plain earnings release (verified by reading each event's own real wire headline before building anything). So this connection is issuer-level, not event-level: these real trials/applications/clearances are separate, dated regulatory context for 6 of the 23 issuers, not a label, score, or reaction driver for any specific M1/M2 event. Full per-study/per-application/per-device classified detail (out/biotech-sponsor-scan.json on the runner) is not uploaded as a workflow artifact and does not survive the job, matching every other M3 workflow's own established pattern -- only the printed by_issuer summary above is a durable record of this specific dispatch.
not_a_claim: Not a claim that these are the only real trials/applications/clearances each company has -- clinical_trials_sponsor_search()/device_sponsor_search() both cap at 20 results per issuer/pathway; ASMB's 20-of-20 clinical-trials result means the true count is >= 20, undercounted here, not fabricated as complete.

Not a claim that a 'matched' result is scientifically or commercially significant, or that a 'not matched' one is irrelevant -- the *_match flags only say whether the source's own recorded sponsor/applicant name plausibly is this issuer; every result is classified and shown either way, never silently dropped.

Not a claim that TECX/ASMB/ACHV have no regulatory activity at all -- zero openFDA drug matches for these three real, clinical-stage companies means nothing has reached FDA-approved status yet, not that no application was ever filed (Drugs@FDA only covers approved/tentatively-approved applications).

Not a claim that LNSR's 14 real 510(k) clearances establish its device's clinical or commercial significance -- decision_category 'cleared' describes only the regulatory outcome (Substantially Equivalent), the same discipline nre.biotech_trials already applies to trial status.

Not a claim that LNSR's zero PMA records means it makes no Class III devices at all industry-wide -- it means only that this specific applicant name has no PMA record in openFDA's own database as of this dispatch.
